cook.title: How to Cook Duck Breast
cook.social_title: Duck breast, cooked in a cold pan
cook.pinterest_title: How to Cook Duck Breast with Crispy Skin (Cold-Pan Method)
cook.primary_image_alt: Sliced duck breast with crisp rendered skin
claims: Place skin-side down in a cold, dry pan.
Bring the heat up gradually over 8–12 minutes.
Pour off fat two or three times during the cook.
Flip when the skin is deep golden-brown, matte and firm.
Insert the thermometer through the side into the thickest part.
Rest 5–8 minutes, skin-side up, uncovered or loosely tented.

temperature.title: Duck Breast Temperature & Doneness
temperature.social_title: What temperature should duck breast be?
temperature.pinterest_title: Duck Breast Temperature Chart: Pull Temps, Carryover & Doneness
temperature.primary_image_alt: Colored-pencil illustration of an instant-read thermometer
claims: Probe through the side, horizontally, into the geometric centre of the thickest part.
Medium-rare: pull at 125–130°F (52–54°C); final 130–135°F (54–57°C).
USDA safe minimum: final temperature 165°F (73.9°C) or above.
Lower-temperature doneness bands are culinary conventions, not safety clearances.
Rest 5–8 minutes; carryover varies with breast size and cooking intensity.

crisp.title: Why Your Duck Skin Isn't Crispy
crisp.social_title: Why your duck skin isn't crispy
crisp.pinterest_title: Why Duck Skin Isn't Crispy — 5 Causes and the Fix for Each
crisp.primary_image_alt: Colored-pencil illustration of duck breast rendering in a pan
claims: Pat the skin fully dry immediately before cooking.
Start in a cold or barely warm pan and raise heat gradually.
Leave visible gaps between pieces.
Pour off rendered fat when it pools around the breast.
Flip when the skin is matte and deep gold, not on a fixed timer.
Score through the fat cap before cooking.
Rest skin-side up, uncovered or loosely tented.

recipe.title: Pan-Seared Duck Breast
recipe.pinterest_title: Pan-Seared Duck Breast Recipe (Crispy Skin, Rosy Centre)
recipe.primary_image_alt: Pan-seared duck breast sliced to show a rosy centre and crisp skin
claims: Score the fat cap and start skin-side down in a cold, dry, unoiled pan.
Render over low heat for 12–18 minutes until thin, deep gold and crisp.
Pull at 130–135°F (54–57°C) for a rosy medium-rare and rest five minutes.
Cook to 165°F (74°C) for the official poultry safety minimum.
